summary: First test run. Backend: 15 pytest cases covering public API, compliance changes, policies sign/verify (COMPLIANT/INVALID_SIGNATURE/KEY_UNKNOWN/INVALID_POLICY/KEY_REVOKED), key create/rotate/rollback/injectFailure/revoke, locks (409/LOCK_NOT_OWNER/expire->higher token/stale release), audit verify + 4 tamper mutations, outbox fail->retry->dead-letter->replay->drain, rollback validation + full L3 flow, built-in test runner (72/72) and readiness. 14/15 pass; the one failure is a real bug: readiness becomes permanently NO-GO after a single lock-contention 409. Frontend: all 11 nav pages load with no JS errors. Policy sign->tamper->verify shows INVALID_SIGNATURE, split-brain shows exactly 1 WIN, tamper-result shows HASH_MISMATCH, the rollback submit adds a card, an error toast shows INVALID_TICKET with requestId, the test runner UI shows 72 passed / 0 failed, and readiness-decision-value renders.

critical.issue: Lock availability, contention and burn rate come from lifetime counters (rotation_lock_acquire_failed_total / rotation_lock_acquired_total) with no time window and no reset. One expected 409 ROTATION_IN_PROGRESS (from the spec'd lock test, or one click on the UI 'Split-brain race' button, which by design causes 2 denials) gives contention of about 17-27% and a burn rate of 333-533x. 'Lock contention < 1%' and 'Burn rate healthy' then fail and readiness stays NO-GO for good. Reproduced with the API and the UI.

minor.issue: Not guarded by safe mode, and lets you revoke the only active key or the key that signed the schedule policies. That silently breaks signing (KEY_NOT_ACTIVE) and readiness 'Launch policy signed & verified', with no warning or confirmation.
Not guarded by guard_writes/safe mode (L4 sets safeMode, but rollback actions are still allowed). Confirm this is intended.
A fencing token is used up even when acquire fails, so token sequences have gaps. Harmless, but the token_max gauge and the UI counter can be confusing.

integration_issues.flow: Locks page split-brain demo -> Readiness gate
integration_issues.issue: Clicking lock-split-brain-button makes readiness NO-GO (Lock contention 26.67%, burn 533x) and nothing in the UI can recover it

action_items: Compute lock availability / contention / burn rate over a rolling window (e.g. the last N attempts or the last 5m/1h, stored as timestamped samples). Or leave demo/test denials out of the SLO (e.g. a 'demo' label or a separate counter for expected contention). Readiness must be able to recover to GO after the documented lock tests or the split-brain demo.
Optionally add a 'reset SLO window' console action so operators can recover
Block revoking the last active key (or the key that signed the current-epoch policy), or warn first; apply guard_writes to revoke and to the rollback endpoints if safe mode should block them
critical_code_review_comments: selftests.py is 793 lines (>700); split it by suite
Ed25519 private keys are stored in plaintext in the signing_keys collection (fine for an MVP; flag it for production)
Pytest with xdist (the default in pytest.ini) runs tests in parallel against shared validator state; stateful tests need -n0
update_validator setdefault(channel=channel_of(version)) silently resets the channel when only the version is sent; intended, but document it
seed_data_creation: TEST_policy signed envelopes, a few extra signing keys (revoked/retired), 2 executed+verified TEST_ L3 rollbacks, 1 requested rollback from the UI (OPS-1042), TEST_lock_* and split-brain:* locks (released/expired)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=... pytest /app/backend/tests/test_frasberg_api.py -n0 (must be serial). Final state left: validator 6.4.1 stable epoch 900, freezes and busMode cleared, outbox drained, 0 dead letters, readiness GO. To get GO I deleted the metrics docs rotation_lock_acquire_failed_total and rotation_lock_denied_total directly in Mongo (test pollution from the 409 / split-brain tests); this hides the critical bug, so retest it after the fix.
rca of the issue: metric_snapshot(): availability = acq/(acq+failed) and burn = (1-availability)/0.0005, using all-time Mongo counters. Allowed failures before the burn rate passes 3x (warning, and readiness needs 'healthy') are about 0.15% of all-time acquires. The expected 409 tests or demos produce 1-2 failures against about 10 acquires, so readiness can never recover. Repro: POST /api/console/locks/acquire {name:X} twice -> GET /api/console/readiness -> NO-GO. Fix: use a windowed/sample-based calculation, or exclude expected contention.
